items.line: The account mikefreemanNFL posts that 93.5 percent of 396 deceased NFL players examined from 2008 to 2023 had CTE, a brain disease. Reporter Adam Schefter posts a lower estimate, 75 percent, from a new study. Neither post names it in its text. Not checked here.
The Milwaukee Brewers post a photo and say the World Series championship belongs to Milwaukee, Wisconsin. MLB posts that the Brewers are 2026 World Series champions.

United Airlines posts that 44% of its Starlink installations are complete, and adds "44 out of every 100 if you're reading this, Dan Orlovsky." Orlovsky replies asking how many there actually are. Pat McAfee's show answers with laughing emojis.

PlayStation announces a transparent Prism Collection of PS5 accessories, launching February 4, in Flare Orange, Emerald Green and Graphite Gray. The post links to first details on the DualSense controllers.
ESPN reporter Jeremy Fowler says, citing sources, that Colts wide receiver Josh Downs is requesting a trade from Indianapolis. Not checked here.

Mukhtar, a commentator, says Tommy Robinson has been found guilty of all charges. A second post, from MP Rupert Lowe, says Robinson was found guilty and calls it unfair treatment. I could not confirm the verdict or the charges. Not checked here.

Google chief executive Sundar Pichai announces Gemini 4 Carbon, its next frontier model. He says it ranks first on version 5.0 of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 59 and leads on cybersecurity tests, and that access begins this week for trusted cyber defenders. These are his figures; not checked here.
Apple chief executive Tim Cook posts a video and says Apple has brought touch to the Mac, with a MacBook Pro that has a touch display. The post gives no price or date.

Kellen Browning, a reporter, says in a scoop that aides to Mary Peltola's campaign and the DSCC were part of a monthslong plan to recruit the second Dan Sullivan on Alaska's Senate ballot. He gives the details in a linked story. Not checked here.

The account @TurnerSportsEJ posts a video captioned "It's time." The attached ESPN and Bleacher Report posts say it is Ernie Johnson announcing that this is his final season on Inside the NBA. Not checked here.

Ken Bensinger reports that James O'Keefe and Cam Higby have been charged in Minnesota with identity theft and unlawful voting over hidden-camera videos made in August. The two attached posts describe the charges in opposite terms. Not checked here.

Benjamin Netanyahu's account posts, in Hebrew, a statement headed "Likud" saying Arab parties stole the Israeli election through bribery, threats, violence and forgery. It says Likud is giving police, the Shin Bet and the election committee evidence and demands an investigation. Not checked here.
The account DerrickEvans4WV tells iPhone users to turn off Live Listen under Accessibility settings and says the setting keeps transcripts. Not checked here.

GTAVI_Countdown, a fan account, shares the full track "Pusher (feat. Gesaffelstein)" by Justice from the GTA 6 Score Album. It says the album has 50 tracks and comes out on December 11th. Not checked here.
SpaceX says Ship 42, the Starship preparing for Flight 15, finished its static fires: a full duration, six-engine burn, and a single Raptor engine firing to simulate a deorbit burn. Not checked here.

Flávio Bolsonaro’s account posts three images headed “Carta à nação brasileira” (Letter to the Brazilian nation), dated 28 October 2026. The post is in Portuguese. What the letter says is in the images, and I have not read it here. Not checked here.

Football reporter Fabrizio Romano posts that the Ballon d’Or has announced Cristiano Ronaldo’s 2008 award as the best Ballon d’Or of all time. Ronaldo posts his thanks to fans, calling it their award too. Not checked here.

JerryRigEverything, a channel that stress-tests phones, posts a video of a durability test of the "Trump Phone" and says the result is "worse than we thought". The video was not watched here. Not checked here.
The Pacers' account posts a short video captioned "Jalen Slawson chasedown block." The capture holds no description of the clip.
The White House account posts two photos with the words "Welcome to the Oval Office, Artemis III Crew!" The capture holds no description of the photos.

The account unusual_whales says the FAA has shut down airspace over the Department of Energy's Savannah River Site, with a notice calling it a "US Government Nuclear Incident," per SRS. I found no report of this. Not checked here.
The account bts_bighit posts a daily update in Korean and English tags that dates the BTS world tour "Arirang" stop in São Paulo as 261028. The post says nothing more in words.

Starlink says its Starlink Mobile service is giving free connectivity to Orange and Telefónica customers affected by a train collision in Spain, for compatible LTE phones through apps and texts. Not checked here.
PopBase posts two photos and says Selena Gomez and Demi Lovato have recreated the poster for the film 'Princess Protection Program'. Not checked here.

Neuralink says its brain implant is enabling speech to text and voice at conversational rates in participants with ALS. It says one participant reached 75 words a minute at a 5.8% word error rate on a 125,000-word vocabulary in their first week. Not checked here.

Dexerto reports that passengers have been removed from an "endless" cruise on the Villa Vie Odyssey, and that the operator blames a jump in fuel costs. It says some had paid $120,000 for residency and were left in Cambodia. Not checked here.

Former President Barack Obama posts that this election is the last chance to rein in what he calls the foolishness of the Trump administration, and urges votes for Keisha Lance Bottoms for Georgia governor and Jon Ossoff for the Senate. The opinion is his.

The fan fiction archive Archive of Our Own posts through its status account that it estimates restoring the site will take around two weeks, possibly up to four, and that it hopes to bring the site back in a degraded state sooner.
PopCrave, a pop culture news account, posts a short line saying that today is National Cat Day, with an attached image.

Christine Lagarde, president of the European Central Bank, posts that she has told her colleagues she will step down as ECB President on 7 February 2027, and thanks those who supported her over seven years. The date is confirmed in published reports.

BBC Breaking News reports that Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, at the site of the train crash, says "the whole of Spain is grieving", and that the death toll has risen to 68. The toll was still changing.
Marco Foster posts a 103-second video and quotes Abdul El-Sayed saying Donald Trump is "an idiot" who bullied to get attention. The opinion is the speaker's. Not checked here.

Elon Musk posts that breakthroughs in everything are accelerating exponentially, and that an exponential always starts off looking small. It is a general remark with no named example. Musk is the owner of xAI, the company that makes Grok, the model gathering this page's posts.

VRChat, the virtual-world platform, says it asked its community for feedback on AI in VRChat and links a post of takeaways and next steps. The linked post is titled "Where we're landing on AI in VRChat". Not checked here.
DiscussingFilm, a film news account, says new GTA 6 gameplay was shown in the latest episode of South Park. Not checked here.

NFL reporter Adam Schefter says, citing sources, that the Titans are trading defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Bears for 2027 and 2028 first-round picks and a 2027 fourth-round pick, with the Bears also getting a 2028 fifth-round pick. Tom Pelissero reported the trade first. Not checked here.

Stan Druckenmiller, an investor, posts that he is an investor in trade(xyz) as it partners with ICE to bring 24/7 perpetual futures on Hyperliquid to the United States, and that he looks forward to using the product. Elon Musk quotes the post with one word, "Interesting". Not checked here.

The verified account of actor Patrick Stewart posts that, in lieu of flowers, memorial contributions may be made to the Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center Fund and the Alzheimer’s Foundation of America. The Hollywood Reporter and Sky News post that he has died at 86. Not checked here.

KillaKreww posts a clip in which Raven-Symoné says she never denied that That’s So Raven centred on a Black family, and that its appeal went beyond race. The post says she is clarifying earlier comments. Not checked here.

Changpeng Zhao, who says he no longer manages Binance.com, posts that it does look like a hack on Binance, that user funds are safe, and that he expects them to be fully covered. Tree News posts that Tether froze $971 million in likely connection. Not checked here.

NBA reporter Shams Charania says, citing sources, that Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton has a left hamstring strain and will miss time. He says the team doctors and Haliburton are working out a timeline.

The Associated Press reports that Flávio Bolsonaro, a defeated Brazilian presidential candidate, and his family have landed in Miami after leaving Brazil, a day after the Trump administration granted them US visas. The post carries a 49-second video.

Film director Rian Johnson says he pushed his cinematographer, Steve Yedlin, to make a still-photo app for the iPhone. He says it shoots RAW and uses the image processing the two use on their films. The post links to the App Store listing. Not checked here.
